363K likes, 1,461 comments - victor.wokmanyama on September 5, 2026: "Chinese Velvet Chicken Breast — So Tender It Melts in Your Mouth!

Full Recipe

Ingredients:

Chicken breast, thinly sliced
½ cup cornstarch
½ tsp baking soda
Green capsicum, finely chopped
Red capsicum, finely chopped
Minced garlic
Chopped spring onion
Sugar
Soy sauce
Oyster sauce
Sea salt
Sesame seeds
Chilli oil, optional
Sichuan peppercorns
Sliced ginger
Cooking wine
Hot oil

Mix the cornstarch with the baking soda, then coat each piece of chicken thoroughly. Cover with cling wrap and pound with a rolling pin until paper-thin and slightly translucent.

Place the capsicum, garlic and spring onion in a heatproof bowl. Pour over hot oil, then add sugar, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sea salt, sesame seeds and optional chilli oil.

Bring a pot of water to the boil with Sichuan peppercorns, spring onion, ginger and cooking wine. Cook the chicken in small batches for about one minute, or until completely white with no pink remaining.

Transfer the chicken directly into the sauce, toss well and serve with steamed rice.

#ChineseFood #ChickenBreastRecipe #HighProteinMeals #EasyDinner #ChineseCooking".

audio.transcript: This is why chicken breast tastes so much better when you cook the Chinese way. It's incredibly tender, almost melts in your mouth, and soaks up all the delicious sauce. It's perfect with rice, but still lean and high in protein, so it's also great if you're working out or trying to lose weight. Start by slicing the chicken breast in a bowl. Combine about half a cup of cornstarch with half a teaspoon of baking soda. Add the chicken and toss until every slice is completely coated. Place the chicken on a chopping board and gently pound it with a rolling pin. Keep pounding until each slice is almost as thin as a towel and slightly translucent. To prevent the chicken from sticking, you can place a cling wrap over it before pounding. Set the prepared chicken aside. In a large bowl, add some finely chopped green capsicum, red capsicum, minced garlic, and chopped spring onion. For a hot oil over the aromatics to release all their flavor. Then add some sugar, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sea salt, and sesame seeds. If you like it spicy, add a little chili oil as well. Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Then add some Sichuan peppercorns, spring onion, ginger, and cooking wine. Add the chicken slices and cook for about one minute. Once the chicken has turned completely white with no pink remaining, remove it from the water. Cook the chicken in several small batches. Don't add too much at once, as you want the water to remain at a steady boil. Finally, add the cooked chicken to the sauce and toss until every slice is evenly coated. You can serve it with steamed rice and enjoy.
